title: Fppf local lifting of a geometric split torus
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Group schemes over $S$ have the multiplication, inverse and identity diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with base $S$. Write $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}_S\mathcal O_S[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units, and let $T=\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$ for $r\geq0$. Let $s\in|S|$, let $\Omega$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of the residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $j_0:\mathbf G_{m,\Omega}^r\hookrightarrow G_\Omega$ be a closed subgroup immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There exist an affine open neighborhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$, an affine scheme $S'$, a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] $p:S'\to S$ factoring through $U$ such that $S'\to U$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and has finite fibres, a point $s'\in S'$ above $s$ with a $\kappa(s)$-embedding $\kappa(s')\hookrightarrow\Omega$, and a closed subgroup immersion $j:\mathbf G_{m,S'}^r\hookrightarrow G\times_S S'$ whose fibre at $s'$, extended along this embedding to $\Omega$, equals $j_0$ as a homomorphism. Here finite fibres means finitely many points with finite residue-field extensions; in particular $p$ is locally quasi-finite and locally of finite presentation. If $S$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $p$ is moreover quasi-compact and of finite presentation over $S$, hence quasi-finite. No reductivity, connectedness, henselian or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf . Proposition 3.1.6, printed pp.83-84, and Proposition 3.1.9 proof (1), first paragraph, printed p.86: finite residue extension, fppf neighborhood, etale lifting and splitting. The quasi-finite refinement uses successive monic polynomial lifts of a finite residue extension before the etale neighborhood.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $s$, and write $\mathfrak p$ for its prime. We work over $U$ and will check the composite to $S$ at the end. The finite intermediate extensions $L/\kappa(s)$ in $\Omega$ form a directed union with colimit $\Omega$. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out] to the homomorphism $j_0$ between the two finitely presented affine schemes over this limit. Descend its multiplication, inverse and identity equalities at a common stage by the equality clause of that node. By [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion], increase the finite field extension once more so the descended homomorphism $i_L:\mathbf G_{m,L}^r\to G_L$ is a closed immersion. Its extension to $\Omega$ is the given map $j_0$, with its original parametrization. The inverse systems and their models are affine, hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; the inverse limit is the spectrum of the field union by the affine spectrum universal property.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.9 proof (1), printed p.86: descent to a finite residue extension; Stacks Tag 01ZM and Tag 01ZP.

proof.text: Write $L$ as a finite tower of simple algebraic extensions of $\kappa(s)$. Starting at $(A,\mathfrak p)$, suppose a prime $\mathfrak q_i$ in a finitely presented algebra $B_i$ has the required intermediate residue field. The finitely many coefficients of the next monic minimal polynomial in $\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)$ are fractions of elements of $B_i/\mathfrak q_i$; invert their denominators, none in $\mathfrak q_i$. Lift the coefficients to this localization and adjoin one root of the monic lift. The map to the next residue field, sending that root to the prescribed generator, has a prime kernel whose residue field is the next field. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] the monic quotient has a finite power basis, so is flat by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat]. Localization is flat because tensoring with a localization is localization, and localization preserves kernels (a zero fraction is killed by one denominator) and cokernels. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] makes the resulting $A\to B$ flat. Each localization and monic adjunction is finitely presented, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] makes $B$ finitely presented over $A$. Every fibre is a succession of localizations of finite-dimensional algebras over the residue field, hence has finitely many points with finite residue extensions. At the final prime $\mathfrak q$, $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=L$ with the specified embedding in $\Omega$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.9 proof (1), printed p.86, fppf residue extension; explicit monic-tower refinement as in Stacks Tag 07NE.

proof.text: Let $H=G\times_U\operatorname{Spec}B$. Smoothness persists under base change by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Apply [lem-sfb-residue-marked-smooth-group-integer-model] to $H$, the prime $\mathfrak q$, and $i_L$. Obtain $B_0\subset B$, $H_0/B_0$, $\mathfrak q_0=B_0\cap\mathfrak q$, and $i_0$ over $k_0=\kappa(\mathfrak q_0)$ whose extension to $L$ is exactly $i_L$. Put $R=(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-g-ring], $B_0$ is a G-ring and thus Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], $R$ is Noetherian. It is a G-ring as well: every prime localization of $R$ is the corresponding prime localization of $B_0$, so the completion maps in [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] are the same maps. The affine smoothness dictionary is [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine].

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6 proof, printed p.84, first reduction to a finite-type integer base with the marked fibre retained.

proof.text: Let $C=\widehat R$ be the maximal-adic completion. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], local with residue field $k_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], and complete by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal]. Base-change $H_0$ to $C$, retaining smoothness by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Apply [lem-sfb-complete-local-split-torus-hom-lift] to the fixed split torus and the specified closed immersion $i_0$. This gives a closed homomorphism $\widehat i:\mathbf G_{m,C}^r\hookrightarrow(H_0)_C$ reducing to $i_0$, without changing its source identification.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6 proof, printed p.84, application of Corollary B.3.5 to the completed local ring.

proof.text: Express $C$ as the directed union of its finite-type $R$-subalgebras. By [thm-pd-spreading-out], the map $\widehat i$ descends to a homomorphism $i_D:\mathbf G_{m,D}^r\to(H_0)_D$ over one such algebra $D$: the multiplication, unit and inverse equalities descend at a common later stage. Increase $D$ once more using [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion] so that $i_D$ is closed. All schemes here are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] as required by both cited statements. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], $D$ has a finite presentation $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. The images $a_i\in C$ of its generators solve the finitely many equations $f_j=0$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6 proof, printed p.84, finite-type subalgebras of the completion and descent before Artin approximation.

proof.text: Choose $h\in B_0\setminus\mathfrak q_0$ clearing the finitely many coefficient denominators of the $f_j$, so that they are polynomials over $B_0[1/h]$. This ring is again finite type over $\mathbf Z$, hence Noetherian and a G-ring by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-z-g-ring]; its localization at $\mathfrak q_0$ is $R$. Apply [lem-trf-artin-approximation-etale-local-map] with $N=1$. Obtain an etale $B_0[1/h]$-algebra $E$, a prime $\mathfrak e$ above $\mathfrak q_0$ with residue field $k_0$, and elements $b_i\in E$ satisfying $f_j(b)=0$ and reducing to the same residues as $a_i$. In $E_{\mathfrak e}$ all elements of $B_0\setminus\mathfrak q_0$ are units; the solution therefore defines an $R$-algebra map $D\to E_{\mathfrak e}$. It has exactly the same reduction $D\to k_0$ as the inclusion $D\subset C$. Base-changing $i_D$ yields a closed homomorphism over $E_{\mathfrak e}$ whose special fibre is $i_0$. Closedness here follows directly by tensoring the surjective map of affine coordinate rings. Closed-immersion base change is [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change].

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6 proof, printed p.84, Theorem 3.1.7 with residue agreement; Stacks Tag 0CAR, N=1.

proof.text: The localization $E_{\mathfrak e}$ is the union of the $E[1/b]$ with $b\notin\mathfrak e$. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out] to spread the preceding map, then its group equalities, over one such principal open. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion] to arrange it is a closed immersion there. Denote this affine etale neighborhood of $\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ by $V$, with distinguished point $v$ and $\kappa(v)=k_0$. It is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}B_0$: the principal opens $\operatorname{Spec}E[1/b]\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B_0[1/h]\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ are open immersions, hence etale, and composites of etale morphisms are etale, both by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2). It is finitely presented over $B_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. Form $S'=V\times_{B_0}\operatorname{Spec}B$. It is affine and etale over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The point $(v,\mathfrak q)$ in the fibre product has residue field $k_0\otimes_{k_0}L=L$, with the chosen inclusion in $\Omega$. Pull back the closed homomorphism on $V$ to get $j$ on $S'$. Tensoring its surjective coordinate map proves closedness; tensoring the group equalities proves it is a homomorphism. At this distinguished point its fibre is $(i_0)_L=i_L$, hence its extension to $\Omega$ equals $j_0$. Affine qcqs hypotheses follow from [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Closed-immersion base change is [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change].

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6 proof, printed p.84, final spreading over an etale neighborhood; then Proposition 3.1.9 proof (1), printed p.86.

proof.text: The map $S'\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale, so flat and locally finitely presented by [def-weil-etale-morphism]; since both schemes are affine it is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. Its fibres are finite, with finite residue extensions, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-quasi-finite]. Compose with $\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$. Using the affine flatness dictionary [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], flatness and finite presentation follow from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. The fibre over any $u\in U$ is the union over finitely many points of the $B$-fibre of their finite etale fibres; residue degrees multiply, so it too has finitely many points with finite residue extensions. The composite $p$ with the open immersion $U\hookrightarrow S$ is flat, since $\mathcal O_{S,u}=\mathcal O_{U,u}$ for $u\in U$ and flatness is a condition on these local rings [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The open immersion is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so lfp, and $p$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]. Its fibres are those above, empty off $U$. Now let $S$ be quasi-separated. For an affine open $W\subseteq S$, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion](1) makes $W\cap U$ quasi-compact, hence a finite union of affine opens $D_k\subseteq U$. Since $S'\to U$ is of finite presentation, hence quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], each $p^{-1}(D_k)$ is quasi-compact, and so is $p^{-1}(W)$. As $U\to S$ is a monomorphism, $S'\times_SS'=S'\times_US'$ is affine, so the diagonal of $p$ is a morphism of affine schemes and is quasi-compact: $p$ is quasi-separated. By the definition recalled in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], $p$ is of finite presentation over $S$, and with its finite fibres it is quasi-finite. The case $r=0$ gives the identity subgroup.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.9 proof (1), printed p.86, composition of the residue extension and etale neighborhood; corrected distinction between local finite presentation and finite presentation over a non-quasi-separated base.

proof_origin.place: Online Proposition 3.1.6 proof and Corollary B.3.5, with explicit marked integer-model reduction, monic residue-extension tower, and correction for non-quasi-separated bases.

The steps are sound: the field descent, the monic tower (it handles inseparable generators), the marked integer model, the complete-local lift (lem-sfb-complete-local-split-torus-hom-lift with f_0=i_0, so the parametrization is kept), spreading out to D, Artin approximation with N=1 and the same residue map, and the étale neighbourhood whose point has residue field k_0⊗L=L. The STATEMENT-DISPUTED change holds: I checked the non-quasi-separated counterexample (eventually-constant-sequence spectrum glued along its open points, rank-2 torus glued by M_n=((1,n),(0,1))). The only citer, reductive-torus-fibre-openness, needs only openness and finite fibres, which remain. New node lem-sfb-residue-marked-smooth-group-integer-model: true (descend the Hopf data, then add the numerators and denominators of the Laurent coefficients, since κ(p) is the directed union of the κ(p_0)); statement-only and strictly smaller than the item; no existing node states it.
